correctness.rationale: For each even n>=4, n-th powers of odd 2-adic units are exactly 1+2^(nu2(n)+2) Z2. The three cases comparing input valuations give B0=1+qZ2, B1=c+qZ2 and B2=1+c+qZ2 after common scaling by 2^(nv), with both inclusions verified. In nonsplit cases all three B_i avoid zero, valuation d_i<h. Their quotients equal explicitly the nine unit-coset balls. The displayed union is locally finite on each nonzero annulus and including zero makes it closed. In split cases a simple 2-adic root gives density. A standalone modular verifier passed 456 finite residue-value checks and 2176 valuation-shell checks, supplementary to the proof.

originality.rationale: The exact nine-coset closure for nonsplit weighted classes c not congruent to ±1 modulo 2^(v_2(n)+2) is not asserted by the inspected density theorem, unweighted sumset work, or searched published records. residual_risks: Non-indexed or implicit existing formula may already give precisely the weighted nine-coset equality.

value.rationale: For a natural infinite two-variable diagonal-form family, the earlier result distinguished only dense/non-dense. The complete nonsplit answer now gives all valuations and all unit congruence classes (the latter invisible in density-only statements) uniformly for every even exponent and odd weight. The exact finite union of local coset balls is a natural topological invariant of interest in p-adic quotient arithmetic; the substantive new cases c not congruent ±1 modulo q are neither arbitrary slices nor mere repeated unweighted tables.
